questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.2 ADK Fundamentals | Self-Test #2 & Trigger #3 | M0L7 Slides 10–12
questions.q: How do ADK workflow agents (SequentialAgent, ParallelAgent, LoopAgent) orchestrate their sub-agents?
options: Using predefined deterministic logic without consulting an AI model to orchestrate (while sub-agents can still be LLM agents and call tools)
By calling an LLM router before every step to decide which sub-agent runs next
By prohibiting sub-agents from using an LLM or calling any tools
By converting all sub-agents into static SQL queries
questions.why: Workflow agents (SequentialAgent, ParallelAgent, LoopAgent) run sub-agents using predefined logic (in order, concurrently, or repeated) without consulting an AI model to orchestrate. Sub-agents can still be LLM agents and call tools.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.2 ADK Fundamentals | Trigger #2 | M0L7 Slide 25
questions.q: A team is building a pipeline where three steps always run in the exact same order and no model is needed to decide the route. Which design pattern should they choose?
options: A deterministic workflow pattern (such as SequentialAgent)
An LLM coordinator pattern, because every routing decision requires a model call
A standalone SkillRevision resource without ADK
An unauthenticated webhook loop
questions.why: Google's design guidance (§1.2): if the steps are predefined and no model needs to orchestrate them, use a deterministic workflow pattern. Use agentic patterns (coordinator) only when the model must decide the route.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.2 ADK Fundamentals | Trigger #1 | M0L6 Slides 6–7
questions.q: When you pass a Python function as an ADK tool, how does ADK build the tool schema that the model sees?
options: From the function's name, docstring, parameters, type hints, and default values
By reading the full Python function body and inline # comments
From a hand-written JSON schema file that you must author manually for every tool
From the function's return statement only
questions.why: ADK builds the tool schema from the function's name, docstring (becomes description), parameters, type hints, and default values. You never hand-write JSON schemas for function tools.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.2 ADK Fundamentals | Trigger #1 | M0L6 Slides 6–7
questions.q: In an ADK Python function tool, which parameters are treated as REQUIRED, and what does the model NEVER see?
options: Parameters without default values are required, and the model never sees the function body or # comments
Parameters with default values are required, and the model reads inline # comments for hints
All parameters are optional, and the model inspects the entire Python function body
Only string parameters are required, and the model ignores the docstring
questions.why: Parameters without default values are marked required in the tool schema; the docstring becomes the tool description; the model never sees the function body or # comments.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.2 ADK Fundamentals | Trigger #3 | M3L1 Slide 9
questions.q: Which node types are supported in an ADK 2.0 graph workflow, and how are parallel branches merged?
options: Functions, human input, Tools, and LLM capabilities (agents), with Join nodes merging parallel branches
LLM agent nodes only; graphs cannot include plain functions or human input
Tools and SQL nodes only, merged by a LoopAgent
Only Model Armor templates and Service resources
questions.why: ADK 2.0 graphs support four node types: Functions, human input, Tools, and LLM capabilities (agents), and use Join nodes to merge parallel branches.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.2 ADK Fundamentals | Trigger #3 | M3L1 Slide 9
questions.q: In an ADK 2.0 graph, what is the difference between setting data on an Event's 'state' field versus using 'output'?
options: Setting an Event's 'state' field lets any downstream node read it, whereas 'output' passes data only to the immediate next node
'output' is readable by all downstream nodes, whereas 'state' only reaches the immediate next node
Both 'state' and 'output' pass data only to the immediate next node
Neither 'state' nor 'output' can pass data between graph nodes
questions.why: Nodes set shared state through an Event's 'state' field so any downstream node can read it. 'output' passes data only to the immediate next node.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.2 ADK Fundamentals | Trigger #5 | M3L1 Slide 10
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a real ADK SessionService implementation (a classic exam distractor)?
options: TextEmbeddingService
InMemorySessionService
DatabaseSessionService
VertexAiSessionService
questions.why: The three real SessionService implementations are InMemorySessionService, DatabaseSessionService, and VertexAiSessionService. 'TextEmbeddingService' is a classic made-up distractor called out in §1.2.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.2 ADK Fundamentals | Trigger #5 | M3L1 Slide 10
questions.q: What does ADK's SessionService do during a conversation?
options: Loads and saves Session objects (one conversation's state and event history) and applies 'state_delta' from each event
Generates vector embeddings for PDF files stored in Cloud Storage
Builds the tool schema from Python docstrings and type hints
Issues 3-legged OAuth tokens for third-party SaaS applications
questions.why: SessionService loads and saves Session objects (state and event history) and applies the 'state_delta' from each event.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.2 & §5 Trigger #2 | M0L7 Slides 15–16
questions.q: A parent Coordinator LLM agent fails to delegate tasks to a specialist sub-agent. What is the most likely fix in ADK?
options: Give the sub-agent a clear, specific 'name' and 'description' in Agent(name=..., description=...)
Rewrite the sub-agent as a C++ binary
Remove the docstring from all Python function tools
Switch from VertexAiSessionService to TextEmbeddingService
questions.why: Per Trigger #2, when an LLM coordinator fails to route to a specialist sub-agent, the sub-agent is missing a clear, specific 'name' and 'description' in Agent(name=..., description=...).

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §5 Trigger #17 | M3L1 Slides 14–19
questions.q: In ADK's before_tool_callback, what happens when the callback returns None versus returning a dict?
options: Returning None allows normal tool execution; returning a dict blocks/short-circuits the tool and returns that dict to the LLM
Returning None blocks the tool call; returning a dict allows normal execution
Returning a dict deletes the current session state
Both None and dict skip the tool call and terminate the agent
questions.why: Per Trigger #17: In before_tool_callback, return None to ALLOW normal tool execution; return a dict to BLOCK/SHORT-CIRCUIT the tool and return that dict directly to the LLM.
